A.explanation: 3 confuses antiquarks with the number of quarks in a baryon or the three light flavours only.

B.explanation: 4 omits two of the six quark flavours and their corresponding antiquarks.

C.explanation: 5 omits one quark flavour, so it undercounts the matching antiquark flavours.

D.explanation: There are six quark flavours, so there are six matching antiquark flavours with opposite charge and baryon number.

hints: Notice the question asks about antiquark flavours, not the number of antiquarks inside one hadron.
Recall the six quark flavours: $up$, $down$, $strange$, $charm$, $bottom$ and $top$.
Think about how each quark flavour relates to an antiquark flavour with opposite quantum numbers.
walkthrough: Identify what flavour means: the type of quark, such as $up$ or $down$, distinguished by charge, mass and other properties.
List the six quark flavours in the Standard Model: $up$, $down$, $strange$, $charm$, $bottom$ and $top$.
Use the particle-antiparticle rule: every quark flavour has a corresponding antiquark flavour with opposite charge, baryon number and strangeness or charm.
Count the pairs one-to-one: six quark types give six antiquark types, such as anti-up, anti-down, and so on.
Match the count of 6 to the listed options. This is option D.
